articleTitle: Clustering Method and Voltage Regulation Strategy for Distribution Networks Based on Voltage Regulation Requirements
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of voltage over-limit caused by large-scale distributed energy access to distribution network, the traditional centralized voltage control method has been difficult to meet the needs of distribution network control and market development. Therefore, a distributed energy cluster voltage regulation control strategy is proposed. Firstly, in order to divide the distribution network into clusters, a k-means clustering algorithm based on electrical distance is proposed to form a distribution network voltage regulation cluster. Then, by using the methods of active power reduction and reactive power regulation, the voltage in the cluster is adjusted by combining the improved particle swarm optimization algorithm with the minimum power regulation and voltage fluctuation as the goal. Finally, the simulation is carried out in the IEEE33 node system to verify the effectiveness of the cluster voltage autonomy strategy.

articleTitle: Economic Dispatch of Integrated Energy Systems Based on Improved Data-driven Adjustable robust model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: To promote wind power consumption and enhance energy efficiency in integrated energy systems, this paper proposes an Imprecise Dirichlet model data-driven two-stage adjustable robust optimization method based on an improved uncertainty set using Wasserstein generative adversarial networks. First, Wasserstein generative adversarial networks is used to expand the historical statistical data set, and the data-driven uncertainty set is constructed to describe the uncertainty of wind power output. Second, to enhance the operational economy of the integrated energy systems, a two-stage adjustable robust economic dispatch model based on improved uncertainty sets is developed. Third, the column and constraint algorithm, duality theory, and Big-M method are employed to solve the two-stage model. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed model and method is validated through the example analysis.

articleTitle: EIMPNet: End-to-End Iterative Feature Matching and Pose Estimation Joint Optimization Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: Traditional pose estimation methods typically involve two separate steps: first using feature matching algorithms to identify matches and then estimating the pose. These conventional approaches often concentrate on enhancing match quality or eliminating potential outlier correspondences, overlooking the inherent connection between feature matching and pose estimation. Therefore, we propose EIMPNet, an end-to-end optimization network for joint feature matching and pose estimation, generating sparse features and pose simultaneously. Specifically, we use an iterative graph neural network to enhance pre-extracted descriptors, facilitating the network in the extraction of robust matches. We embed differentiable pose estimation into the matching network, along with the match loss for training. This strategy enables the network to iteratively predict matches that are more favourable to pose estimation and naturally reduces the impact of outliers. Experimental results on HPatches and MegaDepth datasets show that our end-to-end training enhances pose estimation metrics and efficiency compared to baseline methods, eliminating the need for RANSAC iterations.

articleTitle: Hybrid Energy Storage Capacity Configuration based on Empirical Mode Decomposition for Industrial Park
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: With the popularity of distributed clean energy such as wind and solar in industrial parks, the fluctuating, intermittent and stochastic characteristics of distributed energy bring challenges to energy management. A hybrid energy storage optimal configuration strategy for industrial parks is proposed to address the output fluctuation problem of distributed energy sources. First, empirical mode decomposition is used to allocate the distributed generation original power into supercapacitor power task and lithium battery capacity task. Next, based on the allocation results, a hybrid energy storage optimal configuration model considering the maximum fluctuation quantity constraint with the objective of minimizing the annual comprehensive cost is established. Finally, the proposed configuration strategy is validated and analyzed with an actual industrial park as a case study, and the results show that the proposed capacity configuration scheme can effectively stabilize the fluctuation of distributed power output.

articleTitle: A Low-Cost Deployment Case Study for Industrial IoT Data Collection and Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: Despite the widespread implementation of SCADA systems in factories for centralized data management, their functionality is restricted to devices equipped with sensors. Manual readings are still prevalent for critical instruments like temperature and pressure gauges, lacking interfaces, leading to inefficiencies and errors. Upgrading production line sensors with IoT-enabled instruments is costly and disruptive. To tackle this, we propose a cost-effective data acquisition system that leverages edge acquisition devices and deep learning algorithms without altering the existing equipment and processes. Our solution involves installing new sensors or cameras in critical areas and employing image recognition algorithms alongside indirect measurement techniques. This approach enhances the real-time accuracy of data collection, significantly boosts the overall efficiency of the production process, and reduces operating costs.

articleTitle: An Improved Anti-outlier Robust Square-Root Cubature Kalman Filter Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: An improved anti-outlier robust square-root cubature Kalman filter (SRCKF) algorithm is studied. Based on Scaled-Contaminated Normal Distribution Model (SCNM), the improved anti-outlier robust-SRCKF algorithm is proposed by combining the idea of SCNM model with SRCKF algorithm. The simulation results show that the anti-outlier robust SRCKF algorithm has strong stability and high estimation accuracy, and can better suppress the adverse effects of observation outliers.

articleTitle: Pose recognition initialized pedestrian tracking for drones
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: Pose recognition and object tracking are two classical research topics in computer vision. Recently, pedestrian tracking with consumable drones gets a wide range of applications in aerial photography. In the initialization stage, pedestrian movement in the image causes inaccuracy of the pedestrian bounding box for the tracking algorithm. In this paper, we propose a pose recognition initialized pedestrian tracker for drones. This tracker runs on drone equipped edge computing device. First, the skeleton keypoints are detected by the OpenPose convolutional neural network. Second, the pedestrian pose is recognized according to the spatial distribution of all skeleton keypoints and then triggers the pedestrian tracking algorithm. Last but not the least, the rectangular image region of the pedestrian is fed into the tracking algorithm which leads the drone and camera to follow the pedestrian. Experimental results demonstrate that the pose recognition initialized pedestrian tracker for drones proposed in the paper is more accurate and robust compared with the manually labeled bounding box initialized tracker.

articleTitle: Lightweight Implementation of a Transformer-based Single Image Dehaze Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of information technology, image dehazing technology has become increasingly important in many fields. In recent years, a multitude of new image dehazing methods have been proposed and have been widely applied across various sectors. Currently, as the Transformer architecture grows in popularity, this paper considers integrating the Transformer network structure into the domain of image dehazing. The paper aims to optimize the traditional U-shaped dehazing network that utilizes semantic segmentation by reducing the number of network layers to achieve a lightweight design while also improving the network's dehazing performance. Ultimately, the performance and effectiveness of the proposed network in this paper have been evaluated on typical datasets.

articleTitle: Pixel-level Motion Deblurring Based on Multi-Scale Recurrent Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: Motion deblurring remains a significant challenge in the field of computer vision, with existing methods often struggling to fully restore the sharpness of edge features, resulting in noticeable visual artifacts. In this paper, we propose a novel pixel-level image deblurring method that leverages recurrent recursive networks (RRNs) to address these shortcomings. Our approach is built upon the Self-Residual Network (SRN) architecture, which has demonstrated strong performance in image restoration tasks. We enhance the SRN architecture by introducing a multi-scale fusion mechanism that effectively captures and integrates features at different resolutions, thereby improving the recovery of fine details, particularly in edge regions. Additionally, we streamline the network structure and reduce the number of parameters, making the network more computationally efficient and easier to train. This optimization also enhances the network's capacity to model and fit complex image features, leading to improved deblurring performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms existing approaches in both quantitative metrics and visual quality, offering a promising solution to the persistent problem of motion blur in images.

articleTitle: NeuroCam: A Neuromorphic Intelligent Camera System for Face Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: Neuromorphic chips based on spiking neural networks achieve highly integrated functions of information perception, processing, and learning by mimicking the compact human brain cortex leveraging spatiotemporally sparse spikes towards efficient sensory data representation, transmission and processing. They significantly reduce the computational loads of intelligent systems with improved energy efficiency. In this work, we have developed a low-power and low-cost intelligent camera for human face recognition based on our previously proposed neuromorphic chip. The system could accurately and promptly accomplish the face recognition task at a frame rate of 12.5 fps while consuming a moderate amount of 5.88W power. It realized a 100% precision rate and a 97.50% recall rate.

articleTitle: An Embedded System I/O Isolation Technology for Raspberry Pi
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: Nowadays user’s data in devices is at high risk. To ensure security of program’s runtime environment, Trusted Computing and Trusted Execution Environment(TEE) are proposed, which construct trusted base at the hardware level. Hardware vendors implement hardware trusted base for their new products, Intel’s Software Guard eXtension(SGX) as an example. SGX lacks isolation for device I/O so there are many SGX-based mechanisms proposed that add protection for device I/O. However, all the above trusted mechanisms must be based on that the CPU has extensions for trusted computing, which means that lots of devices equipped with old chips and those embedded devices on other ISA like Arm and RISC-V have no possibility to support this trusted computing mechanism. Therefore, we proposes an I/O isolation technology for embedded devices and implements a trusted computing mechanism named XiRang(eXtended I/O Reliable Authentication Guard) for Raspberry Pi. Specifically, we do the following work. (1) Use an external trusted device as the physical trusted root for embedded devices, which made up for the lack of trusted computing extension of their chips. (2) On the premise of trusted hardware, XiRang realizes the trusted isolation of USB disk, uses trusted Linux container as the application runtime environment, and completes the trusted chain transfer from the external trusted device to the application. (3) Finally, we evaluate performance of XiRang.

articleTitle: A Case Study: Experiment of Artificial Intelligence for Thai Fruit Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: This research uses image processing technology with the deep learning methods, which can simulate the human vision to develop an artificial model for examining and classifying the types of Thai fruit. The experiment is conducted to classify five types of Thai fruits, namely CustardApple, Rambutan, RoseApple, Mangosteen and Durian,. These fruit samples are collected as 300 images of each type in 2D digital photographs from various views. The experimental results shown that the use of deep learning by the convolutional neural network (CNN) based on the model of EfficientNet-B0 architecture provides the excellent classification accuracy at 99%.

articleTitle: MSFusion, A End-to-end SAR And Optical Image Fusion Method
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: With the advancement of remote sensing technology, the application fields of remote sensing images have become increasingly extensive. SAR images contain abundant texture information, while optical images contain a wealth of contour information. Combining the advantages of both can result in images with richer information content. In this paper, we propose a CNN-based SAR image and optical image fusion model, named MSFusion, and compare it with mainstream image fusion algorithms, demonstrating promising results.

articleTitle: PointABM: Integrating Bidirectional Mamba and Multi-Head Self-Attention for Point Cloud Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: In recent years, Transformer has achieved dominance across a multitude of disciplines, attributed to its superior global modeling capabilities. Currently, the Mamba model, distinguished by its linear complexity, is emerging as a formidable challenger. Despite existing advancements, considerable room for improvement remains in point cloud processing, especially within embedded application contexts such as robotic navigation and autonomous vehicles. Based on this observation, we propose PointABM, a hybrid model that integrates Mamba and Transformer architectures to enhance global feature extraction, thereby improving the performance of 3D point cloud analysis. More specifically, first we design a Transformer Block to enhance the representation of global features. Then, we propose a bidirectional Mamba, which comprises both a traditional token forward SSM and an innovative backward SSM. Experimental results demonstrate that integrating Mamba with Transformer significantly enhances the model’s capability to analyze 3D point clouds, offering substantial improvements in both efficiency and accuracy for critical applications.

articleTitle: A Reliable Artificial Intelligence System Architecture Based on Knowledge Reasoning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) technology is rapidly advancing and gradually sweeping into various domains, bringing profound changes to production and daily life. However, with the opportunities presented by AI technology come inherent risks. Ensuring AI is safe, reliable, and controllable to enhance users’ confidence is crucial for the long-term development of AI. Developing trustworthy AI involves focusing on aspects such as reliability, interpretability, fairness, robustness, and privacy protection. It is of paramount importance to constructing a reliable class of AI systems. Addressing the reliability issues prevalent in current widely deployed AI systems, this paper proposes an architecture for a reliable AI system based on knowledge reasoning. The aim is to achieve efficient, accurate and reliable knowledge processing and reasoning. AI-Math, a knowledge graph-based question-answering system developed according to this architecture, serves as an effective application example of reliable artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: Optimizing Cloud Cloud Resource Allocation and Power Management: Attentive-Mamba and Reinforcement Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: The high investment cost with low resource utilization has been a major concern for cloud providers. The efficient operation of clusters and achieving stable and accurate task load predictions are crucial. We introduce Attentive-Mamba, a specialized time series prediction model based on Mamba, designed for accurate cluster workload forecasting, surpassing current benchmarks like the Transformer model in specific tasks. Additionally, we present the RL-based Power Control Policy (RPCP), which autonomously adjusts server power states based on predictive load information, effectively reducing energy consumption while meeting latency requirements. Our study evaluates various VM resource allocation algorithms, identifying approaches that optimize power consumption and latency tradeoffs under ideal conditions. Experimental results on real workload traces show that our proposed Attentive-Mamba predictor and RPCP significantly improve the energy efficiency of the data center and maintains the required cloud system performance compared to some other VM consolidation algorithms.

articleTitle: Efficient Spatio-Temporal Out-of-Distribution Detection for Autonomous Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: Learning-enabled components (LECs) are increasingly deployed in autonomous systems to provide adaptive and intelligent decision making in a complex dynamic environment. However, most LECs are typically data-driven, and they may exhibit erroneous predictions impacting system safety when there are some distribution shifts between real testing scenarios and training scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an efficient spatio-temporal Out-of-Distribution (OOD) detection scheme for time-series data to improve the detection performance and robustness over the state-of-the-art. Specifically, the optical flow method is employed to extract the spatio-temporal features in the high-dimensional time series data, and the extracted spatio-temporal optical flow features are encoded with the variational autoencoder to obtain input manifold for the OOD detection. Moreover, we proposed a martingale-based inductive conformal anomaly detection method to achieve lower bounded false alarms owing to the statistical foundation and robustness characteristic of martingale. The experimental evaluation demonstrates that our proposed approach significantly outperforms the existing methods in terms of detection capability and robustness.

articleTitle: Construction Methods of Defective datasets for Deep Learning Vision Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: In response to the lack of defective datasets for deep learning vision algorithms, we researched methods for constructing such datasets. We analyzed the reasons behind the failures of deep learning vision algorithms and summarized 18 types of defects that lead to these failures. These defects were categorized into four major types: dataset, algorithm training, algorithm inference, and algorithm deployment. We constructed 266 defective datasets based on six typical vision tasks: image classification, object detection, object tracking, object extraction, semantic segmentation, and image fusion. Through comparative experiments, we verified the impact of these defective datasets on the performance of various vision algorithms.

articleTitle: Event-Driven Fault Injection Testing Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: As a highly complex embedded system, an autonomous driving system integrates key technologies such as sensors, perception, planning, and control to accomplish crucial tasks like real-time environmental perception, path planning, and vehicle control. Due to the complexity and variability of environmental information, the perception module is prone to generating fault information and transmitting it to the planning control module. This can lead to erroneous decisions and control commands by the planning control module, ultimately causing accidents. Therefore, it is crucial to test the tolerance of the planning control module to fault information. This paper proposes an event-driven fault injection testing framework that can dynamically inject various types of faults based on different fault trigger conditions in the scenario. This approach effectively evaluates the performance of autonomous driving systems under diverse fault conditions. The experimental results show that the framework successfully achieves dynamic fault injection and can clearly define the fault tolerance boundaries of the planning control module.

articleTitle: Construction of a Reliability Measurement Scheme for Deep Learning Vision Algorithms based on Failure Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: With the application of vision algorithms in multitask scenarios such as image classification, object detection and object tracking, the traditional software reliability measurement scheme is difficult to meet the needs of new technologies. Therefore, the research related to the reliability measurement of deep learning vision algorithms has become an urgent need. In this paper, we collect and analyse failure cases in five vision application scenarios, such as image classification, object detection, object tracking, and semantic segmentation, to carry out failure analysis and fault tree analysis. Using the defective causes of the failure cases, ten reliability measurements of deep learning vision algorithms are established, covering four stages: dataset, algorithm training, algorithm inference and algorithm deployment. Through experiments, the influence of each index in the reliability measurement scheme was analysed. The experimental results show that all the measurements in the reliability measurement scheme constructed in this paper have a certain degree of influence, and the three measurements of data balance defect, interference data, and data accuracy defect have the highest influence on the vision task.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Identification Method of Radio-Frequency Fingerprint Based on Deep Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: The development of radio frequency fingerprint recognition technology is becoming increasingly mature, with abundant research and applications confirming the reliability of supervised radio frequency fingerprint technology. However, in real electromagnetic environments, particularly in areas such as intrusion detection and military confrontation, it is not always feasible to collect and analyze target signals in advance, manually annotate them, and enter the annotated signals into a fingerprint database, as obtaining authentic information about the target devices is often challenging. Additionally, unsupervised clustering of radio frequency fingerprints can identify the number of source devices, effectively detecting impersonation and identity-simulation attacks in wireless network security. In summary, research on unsupervised electromagnetic target blind recognition technology based on radio frequency fingerprints holds significant practical application significance. The method of electromagnetic target identification based on deep clustering aims to extract more effective radio frequency fingerprint features, considering the temporal characteristics of I/Q signals. This approach significantly enhances the precision of target recognition without requiring prior labeling, demonstrating superior performance in practical applications such as wireless network security, intrusion detection, and military operations. This method significantly improves the classification accuracy of radio frequency signals in real-world environments compared to previous studies.

articleTitle: Joint Optimization of Service Caching and Task Scheduling in Energy-Efficient Mobile Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: This paper studies an energy-efficient task scheduling problem that takes into account the cooperation among service caching-enabled mobile edge computing (MEC) servers. We consider a MEC system consisting of multiple sub-networks of MEC nodes and formulate the studied problem as a constrained optimization model that makes decisions on energy-efficient assignment of task requests. To cope with the formulated optimization problem, we propose a metaheuristic approach that is built upon the searching mechanism of the squirrel search algorithm (SSA) but involves improved operators and name the metaheuristic approach ISSA. By using an offloading sequence (i.e., a permutation of all computation tasks) to represent the scheduling solution, ISSA uses a cooperative task assignment heuristic for evaluating the fitness value of each candidate solution. This heuristic is responsible for dispatching each task in the sequence to a certain MEC node within the sub-network or outsourcing the task to the cloud in case of insufficient resources, such that the total energy consumption can be calculated. In addition, when updating the squirrel positions to facilitate the metaheuristic search, we employ a new updating rule to enhance ISSA’s capability in exploring the solution space. We perform extensive simulations to demonstrate the advantage of our proposed ISSA over other metaheuristic approaches in reducing the total energy consumption.

articleTitle: Universal Adversarial Attack for Trustworthy LiDAR based Object Detection in Embedded Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: 3D object detection based on deep neural networks (DNNs) has widely been adopted in the field of embedded applications, such as autonomous driving. Nonetheless, recent studies have demonstrated that LiDAR data tends to exhibit intense corruptions, resulting in the failure of 3D object detection tasks. Considering the vulnerability of existing DNNs and the wide applications of 3D object detection to safety-critical scenarios, the robustness of deep 3D detection models under adversarial attacks is investigated in this work. The proposed universal adversarial attack is encoded into a perturbation voxel, which adds point-wise perturbations to benign LiDAR scenes. The detector-level perturbation voxel is generated by suppressing the detector's predictions on training samples, which covers the entire perceptual range of the detector. The designed perturbation voxels can be applied to the entire scene to simulate the global perturbation inherent in LiDAR. And it can adapt to other detectors with various point cloud representations, which makes attack universal. To test the effectiveness of the proposed attack, it was launched against a number of deep 3D detectors using several datasets. The results demonstrate its superiority over existing art.

articleTitle: On the Accurate and Robust Prediction of Optimal Read Voltages in 3D NAND via Data Augmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: With the exponential growth of data, the demand for storage capacity is constantly increasing, leading to the widespread adoption of 3D NAND flash memory in enterprise storage and data centers. However, 3D NAND flash memory faces reliability issues, necessitating the accurate calibration of read voltages to reduce the raw bit errors of read data. For a new chip model, extensive testing is typically required to obtain the optimal reading voltage (ORV) under various disturbance conditions, such as program/erase (P/E) cycles, to adapt to complex real-world scenarios. To reduce such costs, existing research has proposed applying machine learning models to predict the ORV with certain testing data or to fit the changing trend of ORV. In this paper, we first conduct a study on the prediction performance of these models, which shows that they all fall short in accuracy when the training data is limited. To deal with the challenge of limited test data, we propose to accurately and robustly predict the ORV of high-density 3D NAND flash memory through data augmentation in data-scarce scenarios. Specifically, with limited test data, we employ fitting techniques to estimate the ORV under P/E cycles that are not tested for data collection. With the test data and augmented data, we utilize machine learning models, including random forest (RF), support vector machine (SVM), and neural network (NN), for training and prediction. Experimental results on real-chip test data demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves the prediction performance, where the predicted ORV is very close to the ideal ORV.

articleTitle: Causality Extraction based on Sequence Tagging with Triple Attention for Cyber Physical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: Causality extraction from noisy texts for cyber physical applications has long been a challenging task. In this paper, we propose an enhanced BiLSTM-CRF sequence tagging model that achieves state-of-the-art results. Specifically, we extend the multi-head self-attention mechanism by integrating the Coordinate Embedded Channel Attention (CECA) module into the Scaled Dot-Product Attention. Within the CECA module, we innovatively formulate the forward and backward outputs of the BiLSTM layer as two channels to make flat text three-dimensional, subsequently enhancing attention mechanisms inspired by image processing techniques. Experiments conducted on the extended SemEval 2010 Task 8 dataset have demonstrated the effectiveness of our approach, achieving a precision of 84.46%, a recall of 84.79% and an F1-score of 84.62%, surpassing all other comparative models.

articleTitle: A SAR Image Speckle Suppression Method Based on Transformer and Frequency Features
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image speckle is a type of image noise caused by the coherence of terrain, which can degrade the resolution and detection capability of SAR images. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a speckle suppression network based on Transformer and frequency features. The network first performs initial denoising on the images, followed by wavelet transformation to retain high-frequency information, and then inputs the results into the network to guide speckle removal. The main body of the network employs Transformer as the encoder for feature extraction, facilitating better learning of the relationships between different regions. Experiments conducted on both synthetic and real datasets validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, showing superior performance compared to existing classical methods.

articleTitle: Dual-layer Trading Mechanism in the Day-ahead Market Considering Energy Storage as Flexible Ramping Product
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: With the large-scale integration of wind and solar power into the power grid, their volatility and uncertainty pose significant challenges to the flexible and safe operation of the power system. In order to achieve flexible operation of the power system and fully tap into the flexible regulation ability of the power system. A market trading mechanism model considering demand side flexibility resources has been proposed. Firstly, explore the potential and market behavior of demand side flexibility resources; Establish a game model that considers the participation of flexible ramping products(FRP) and new energy generation companies in the day ahead market by comprehensively analyzing and determining the providers of flexible ramping products; Finally, the effectiveness of the model was verified through case studies.

articleTitle: Reliability Evaluation of Security and Stability Control System in Power Grid Based on Dynamic Bayesian Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: The control and safety technologies of the power grid are crucial for its overall security and reliability. Consequently, the reliability of the security and stability control system (SSCS) has become a core concern in the industry because it serves as the second line of defense for the power grid. However, existing methods for quantitatively evaluating the reliability of SSCS are still immature. Therefore, A reliability evaluation method for SSCS based on a dynamic Bayesian network (DBN) is proposed in this paper, which can quantitatively evaluate the dynamic temporal issues during system operation. First, the hierarchical structure and failure modes of the SSCS are analyzed, and a fault tree model for the SSCS is established. Then, using the dynamic fault tree as a bridge, a DBN model is derived from the fault tree. Finally, a reliability evaluation method of the SSCS is built by proposing interval-valued fuzzy numbers to address the issue of insufficient component failure data. Case studies are performed to verify the validity and accuracy of this method.

articleTitle: CenterUNet: a Model Fused Semantic Segmentation for Flange Center Point Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: In the flange segment assembly process of the shipbuilding industry, the accurate detection of the flange’s center point is a key technical challenge for improving the precision and efficiency of automated assembly. Traditional methods rely on manual detection, often limited by insufficient detection accuracy, resulting in low assembly efficiency and unstable precision. To address these issues, this paper proposes a deep learning model combining image semantic segmentation with regression algorithms, called CenterUNet. The model first effectively separates tar-get objects from backgrounds through image segmentation technology, significantly reducing environmental interference. It then uses an optimized regression algorithm to precisely calculate the coordinates of the flange center points, breaking through the recognition limitations of traditional methods in environments. The main advantages of CenterUNet lie in its outstanding accuracy and efficiency. Compared to ResNet18,VGG and EfficientNetV2, our model not only achieves significant improvements in the accuracy of flange center point detection but also shows significant enhancements in stability and robustness. This holds significant practical significance and application value for advancing intelligent manufacturing and automated assembly.

articleTitle: Ground moving target detection using two high-resolution aerial images: theory and methods
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: In drones, high-resolution aerial images can provide a wider field of view and higher spatial resolution than aerial videos. This article investigates the problem of moving target detection using two high-resolution aerial images. We first design a motion quantity based on photogrammetry theory. It is determined by the sensor's intrinsic and extrinsic parameters and target trajectories. Furthermore, the Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB) of motion quantity is given, which is verified by simulation experiments. To solve the moving target detection issue, we propose a method based on hypothesis testing, involving testing whether the motion quantity conforms to a hypothesis at a specified confidence level to determine its motion properties. Finally, through extensive experiments, the performance of our method was assessed. The results conclusively showed that when the confidence level is 95%, the accuracy is 97.68%, precision is 95.10%, recall is 82.20%, achieving a good balance between precision and recall.

articleTitle: STTSBI: A Fast Inference Framework for Small Object Detection in Ultra-High-Resolution Images
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: Ultra-high-resolution images (UHR images), such as satellite images, aerial photographs, and panoramic images, provide high-quality detection information that enhances small and distant object detection performance. However, UHR images often contain hundreds of millions of pixels, leading to considerable inference time with existing frameworks. To address the aforementioned issue, we extend the YOLOv8 network and propose a novel tiling-based object detection framework called Selective Tiling and Two-Stage Batch Inference (STTSBI). In this framework, the input image is first divided into tiles. Then the inserted pre-classification (PCLS) module filters out tiles without target objects and a two-stage batch inference process is employed to enhance GPU utilization efficiency by maintaining batch processing throughout the entire workflow, thereby significantly reducing inference time. According to our experimental setup, our proposed model can infer an image with over a hundred million pixels in no more than 0.4 seconds, achieving a 10× to 40× increase in inference speed compared to the existing methods. Furthermore, we apply binary quantization to the backbone module of YOLOv8 based on the PhoneBit framework, which further reduces the inference consumption. The binary quantization model achieves a 2× speedup compared to the fullprecision model.

articleTitle: ERSCHED: An Efficient and Reliable Scheduler for Workflows in Multi-Edge Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: With the rise of edge computing, many users are turning to hosting and running workflow applications in multi-edge environments. This approach can effectively address issues such as resource limitations, low reliability, and high costs that are often encountered in single-edge environments. However, the heterogeneity of resources in multi-edge environments and the differences among edge service providers (in terms of technical architectures, service types, pricing models, etc.) make scheduling tasks in a multi-edge system quite complex. As a result, effectively utilizing multi-edge resources to efficiently and reliably schedule and execute workflows has become a crucial challenge in multi-edge environments. This paper concentrates on the multi-objective workflow scheduling optimization problem when facing reliability constraints in multi-edge environments. We design an efficient and reliable scheduler, namely ERSCHED, for executing workflows in multi-edge systems, with the goal of optimizing makespan and cost simultaneously under reliability constraints. We implement extensive experiments on both real-world and synthetic workflows to validate the efficacy of our scheduler ERSCHED. Simulation results show that ERSCHED can derive better makespan-cost trade-off fronts with significantly higher HyperVolume than similar peer methods. The average improvement of HyperVolume realized by ERSCHED is 48.7%.

articleTitle: Dynamic Modeling and Functional characterization of NiTi Shape Memory Alloy Spring Actuator for Embedded Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: Shape Memory Alloy (SMA) actuators have attracted significant attention in the field of non-conventional actuators widely used in embedded systems, due to their unique characteristics such as high-power-to-weight ratio, low driving voltages, and ability to produce large strains. However, achieving precise motion control of SMA actuators poses a challenge due to their complex thermostatically behavior and inherent nonlinear hysteresis. In this paper, the Hammerstein-Wiener black-box modeling technique is proposed to accurately predict the nonlinear behavior of the shape memory alloy actuators. The approach utilizes system identification techniques to develop a dynamic model for the SMA spring actuator, which can predict its behavior accurately under various input conditions. This methodology shifts the challenge of accurately modeling the system’s physics to the task of formulating an input-output structure that encompasses its dynamics. The results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed model in precisely forecasting the behavior of SMA actuators, thus aiding in the selection and optimal tuning of control system parameters.

articleTitle: Energy Router Planning Strategy for Distribution Networks Based on Source-Load Matching
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Technology and Embedded Systems (ICITES)
abstract: Energy routers, as an emerging means of current control, can effectively improve the network transmission loss of distribution networks as well as the problem of distributed power consumption. However, the planning of energy routers involves more variables, which are less concerned in current research. In this regard, based on the autonomous partitioning of distribution networks containing Distributed Generation (DG), a two-stage planning model for energy routers considering the matching of source/load barycenter in subregions of distribution networks is proposed to configure the access locations, connection lines, and port capacities of energy routers in distribution networks. Based on the improved IEEE 33-node system, the effectiveness of the proposed energy router planning method is verified, which can effectively improve the distributed power consumption rate of the distribution network and optimize the system operation economy through the optimal configuration of energy routers.
